cards.title: Introduction to APIs in React
cards.content:
In modern web development, React components often need to fetch data from external servers using APIs (Application Programming Interfaces).

React itself doesn't have a built-in HTTP client, so we rely on standard browser APIs like fetch or third-party libraries like Axios to retrieve data.

// Simple fetch call
fetch('https://api.example.com/data')
  .then(response => response.json())
  .then(data => console.log(data));

cards.title: Data Fetching with useEffect
cards.content:
API requests are considered 'side effects' because they interact with the outside world. In React, side effects are performed inside the useEffect hook.

Always provide a dependency array to prevent infinite fetch loops!

useEffect(() => {
  fetch('https://api.example.com/users')
    .then(res => res.json())
    .then(data => setUsers(data));
}, []); // Empty array ensures this runs once on mount

options.text: The API request runs on every single component re-render.
The API request runs only once when the component mounts.
The API request runs only when the state changes.

content.text: Inside useEffect, to ensure an API call only runs once when the component mounts, pass an empty [blank] array as the second argument.

cards.title: Handling Loading and Error States
cards.content:
Users have varying internet speeds. Always manage three states when fetching data:

  • Data: The actual payload returned from the API.
  • Loading: A boolean indicating if the request is in progress.
  • Error: An object or string capturing any network or server failures.

items.text: Set loading state to true and error to null
Await response and parse it into JSON
Save the parsed data to your component state

cards.title: Axios vs. Fetch API
cards.content:
While fetch is built into browsers, Axios is a popular lightweight library. Axios simplifies code because it automatically transforms JSON data and throws errors for non-2xx status codes instantly.

// Axios syntax is cleaner
import axios from 'axios';

axios.get('/api/users')
  .then(response => setUsers(response.data))
  .catch(error => console.error(error));

cards.title: Match the Technology with its Feature

pairs.right: Native browser API; requires manual .json() parsing step
Third-party client; features automatic JSON transformation
Used to cancel pending network requests on unmount
React Hook where component side-effects are executed

cards.title: Cleaning Up and Aborting Requests
cards.content:
If a component unmounts before an API request completes, updating state can cause memory leaks. We resolve this by cancelling the request in the useEffect cleanup function using an AbortController.

useEffect(() => {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  
  fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal })
    .then(res => res.json())
    .then(data => setData(data));

  return () => controller.abort(); // Cleanup
}, [url]);
